top_choice_rationale: P001 awards a single, cleanly attributable invention: the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, concept) and its realisation at the 10^-18 level (Ye). The result is mature and reproduced across independent laboratories, the two-name allocation follows the structure of the achievement, and the citation is scoped to the clock itself rather than to precision spectroscopy, keeping it distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a genuine new phenomenon with a prediction followed by experiment, but the pairing mechanism remains unsettled and the credit split between the 2011 theory and the experiments is harder to draw, so I rank it second ahead of no award. P000 is last because a mature candidate with broad committee support exists.
recusal_note: Research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during my doctorate (field proximity to precision laser spectroscopy near the optical clock work) and WACQT management; no direct collaboration, joint publication or institutional tie to Katori, Ye or the B022 candidates is apparent from the profile, so no recusal appears required.
